stories.headline: NATO jet shoots down Ukrainian drone over southern Estonia; Baltic states accuse Russia of deliberately guiding drones into NATO airspace
stories.summary: On May 19, a Romanian Air Force F-16 operating under NATO's Baltic Air Policing mission shot down a Ukrainian drone near Lake Võrtsjärv in southern Estonia — the first time Estonia has downed a drone entering its airspace. Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur defended the decision and held a press conference with Air Force commander Brigadier General Riivo Valge. In the days that followed, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna accused Russia of electronically steering Ukrainian military drones toward NATO territory to undermine allied support for Ukraine; Baltic presidents including Alar Karis issued a joint declaration urging NATO to upgrade Baltic Air Policing to a full air-defense mission with counter-drone capabilities; and eight Nordic-Baltic foreign ministers issued a joint statement condemning a Russian and Belarusian disinformation campaign about the incidents.

stories.headline: Tsahkna courts India as strategic partner, calls for New Delhi to pressure Russia on Ukraine peace
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna hosted Indian journalists in Tallinn and gave extensive interviews to Indian media around May 20, calling India a 'very important partner' and urging New Delhi to use its diplomatic leverage to pressure Putin to end the war in Ukraine. He also invited Prime Minister Modi to visit Estonia and highlighted growing cooperation in digital governance, AI, and cybersecurity. Indian Ambassador Ashish Sinha separately framed Estonia as a potential gateway to northern European markets for Indian businesses following the EU-India FTA process.

stories.headline: Kevadtorm 2026: Estonia's largest annual military exercise underway with president and EDF commander visiting troops
stories.summary: Kevadtorm 2026 (Spring Storm), the Estonian Defence Forces' largest annual military exercise, ran from early May through approximately June 1, involving conscripts, reservists, Kaitseliit volunteers, and allied troops. President Alar Karis and EDF Commander Lieutenant General Andrus Merilo visited the exercise to review units and operations. Kaitseliit and the Police and Border Guard Board conducted night patrols in southern Estonian towns, and defence education teachers voiced complaints about the new field camp arrangements organized by Kaitseliit.

stories.headline: Reform Party's ratings slide; Michal's party congress speech draws editorial debate and opposition attacks
stories.summary: Prime Minister Kristen Michal delivered a speech at the Reform Party general assembly in which he framed the party against a 'conservative octopus' of opposition parties. An ERR political analyst assessed the party's support would likely recover but not enough to win the next spring's Riigikogu election, with current polling showing Michal as one of the least preferred prime ministerial candidates. Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu attacked the speech in a sharp op-ed, while Reform Party MPs published defences and regular party communications on the party website.

stories.headline: Eesti Pank survey shows average Estonian household net wealth rose 16% in real terms to €103,300 since 2021
stories.summary: The Bank of Estonia (Eesti Pank), in a joint survey with Statistics Estonia using the ECB's Household Finance and Consumption Survey methodology, published results showing average Estonian household net wealth reached €103,300 in 2024, up from €66,200 in 2021. The richest 5% hold 40% of total assets. The survey found households diversifying into investment funds and shares beyond bank deposits, while median households hold liquid assets equivalent to roughly two months' gross income.

stories.headline: LHV Pank restructures: two board members exit as bank pivots to product-based international model; crypto license granted
stories.summary: LHV Pank announced an organisational restructuring intended to move toward a modern product-based management model for international banking. Retail banking head Annika Goroško and IT director Jüri Heero are leaving the board. Separately, the Financial Supervision Authority granted LHV Pank a licence to offer crypto-asset custody and order services under EU MiCA regulation, making it the second licensed crypto-asset service provider in Estonia.

stories.headline: Local government political turbulence: Võru city government falls; Hiiumaa mayor faces no-confidence; EKRE councillors in legal disputes
stories.summary: Multiple Estonian local government stories ran this week. In Võru, the city council voted out the mayor and deputy council chair (both SDE), with a new coalition being formed by Keskerakond, Isamaa, EKRE, and Reform. In Hiiumaa, six EKRE and Isamaa members filed a no-confidence motion against the SDE mayor. In Pärnu, an EKRE city councillor's police fine for conflict-of-interest violations reached the Supreme Court. A Viljandi story involved a Reform mayor giving a bonus to a city official via what critics claimed was a workaround.

stories.headline: Estonian Artists' League loses 700,000 euros to phone fraud scam
stories.summary: The Estonian Artists' League (EKL) lost approximately 700,000 euros through a phone fraud scheme in which scammers impersonating bank and Eesti Pank officials convinced staff to enter PIN codes during a fake cyber-attack alert. The funds were intended for artist salary payments and creative grants; the league announced it may need to sell assets to meet its obligations and filed a police report.
